not reckoning oneself as possessing insight is the practice of wisdom.
Constant diligence in one's own person is the root of wisdom.
To cultivate practices for the sake of sentient beings is the work of wisdom;
To uphold the treasury of all dharmas is the root of knowledge;
To clearly understand the conduct of sentient beings is the work of wisdom.
To deliver all from every evil is the root of wisdom;
To lead sentient beings to the three refuges is the work of insight.
Generous giving constitutes benevolence; Impartially establishing benefit for sentient beings,
To transform others so they leave behind defilement is the work of wisdom;
to benefit all equally, regarding them as possessing the merit of a Buddha—
such is the true practitioner, and this is the work of wisdom.
To fear all that is ablaze and burning is the root of wisdom;
to contemplate that which arises from it is the work of insight.
To attain the wisdom of the exhaustion of anger is the root of wisdom.
To give rise to the wisdom of non-arising is the activity of wisdom;
if one attains the patience regarding sounds and echoes, this is the root of knowledge.
When one’s conduct accords with what has been contemplated, this is the activity of wisdom.
To attain the patience of compliant gentleness is the root of wisdom;
the patience regarding that which is unborn is the work of insight.
To abide in the stage of non-retrogression is the root of wisdom.
Attaining the stage of *avaivartika* is the work of wisdom;
sitting beneath the Bodhi tree is the root of knowledge.
Having attained all supernormal powers (*abhijñā*) is the work of wisdom.
Calculating the root of this wisdom, it is called the mind of the Way;
relying upon this mind, all that one does constitutes the karma of wisdom.
Constantly dwelling with clarity in the mind of the Way, one is then able to remain unmoved and unswerving.
This karma is the work of wisdom, its practice always in accord with the times.
If one cultivates the Buddha-way, this mind is the root of the Way;
such is the Buddha’s spiritual power, as well as his analytical eloquence.
If one were to praise these meritorious achievements—
the Buddha’s virtues and his radiance— for countless eons, one could never reach their limit.
As it was with all the Buddhas of the past, so it is with those of the present.
If one should dwell securely in the future throughout the incalculable ten directions,
and should wish to make offerings to these immeasurable and most supreme ones,
one should follow the path of the Bodhicitta; thus, one will achieve freedom from negligence.

When the Buddha spoke of this wisdom, its fundamental nature, and its karmic activity, the immeasurable buddha-fields of the ten directions shook in six ways, and the precious, adorned high seats did likewise.
Thereupon, the Bodhisattva Prajñākūṭa came forward and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"Indeed, World-Honored One!

For what reason do the countless, incalculable Buddha-lands throughout the worlds of the ten directions now tremble in six ways, and why is it that the high seats established within the void likewise do so?"
The Buddha said,
"Son of good family!
This essential chapter of the sūtra on the fundamental wisdom and karma of knowledge was praised and expounded by the Tathāgatas of the past."
In ages past, when the Bodhisattva Jñānakūṭa was in the void, he offered much protection and inquiry to the Tathāgata; the Buddha then provided him with explanations and answers.
For this reason, the earth shook greatly and a brilliant light shone everywhere.

Chapter 26: The Chapter on Bodhisattva Jñānakūṭa The Great Compassion Sutra, Chapter Twenty-Six: The Chapter on Bodhisattva Jñānakūṭa At that time, there was a bodhisattva named Vibhajyapratibhāna who came forward and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“For what reason is the bodhisattva named Jñānakūṭa?”
The Buddha addressed the son of noble family:

"In the distant past, long ago, there was a Buddha named Śūnyatāśānti Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, Buddha, Bhagavān."
The world was called *Vīryavat* (Diligent), and the eon was named *Āmalaka*.
That Buddha-world was peaceful, secure, and joyful, and its sentient beings were free from affliction.
Under the Tathāgata Śamaśirṣa, there were forty-two thousand bodhisattvas and eighty-four thousand śrāvakas, all of whom were respectful, humble, and compliant with the teachings.
The eloquence of that Buddha, through the Vaipulya sutras, raised ten billion challenges for the sake of the bodhisattvas; with songs and verses, he fully proclaimed to all the bodhisattvas:
"O you true gentlemen!..."
"Who is capable of enduring ten billion difficult questions, explaining each one in detail,
and resolving them? Those bodhisattvas then replied to the Buddha,
"Once this night has passed, we shall resolve them."
Some said seven nights, some half a month, and some a month; only after reflection were they able to dismiss him.
Each reflected for themselves and reported their understanding to the World-Honored One.
At that time, there was a bodhisattva in that assembly named Bodhy-artha who came forward and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“I pray only this, O Great Sage!

Without rising from my seat, without adjusting my deportment, and without further deliberation, may the World-Honored One bear witness before the Tathāgata as I shall resolve all difficult points of meaning.”
At that time, as this noble being uttered this lion’s roar, the trichiliocosm shook in six ways;
a great radiance shone universally throughout the world, and by means of this majestic light, he addressed the terrestrial deities,
the gods of the Four Great Kings, the Trāyastriṃśa gods, the Yāma gods, the Tuṣita gods, the Nirmāṇarati gods, and the [Paranirmita-vaśavartin] gods.
Īśvara, up to the gods of the Māra realm, the Brahmā gods, the Brahmakāyika gods, the Brahmapurohita gods,
the Mahābrahmā gods, the Ābhāsvara gods, the Parīttābha gods, the Apramāṇābha gods, the Ābhāsvara gods,
the Śubhakṛtsna gods, the Parīttaśubha gods, and the Apramāṇaśubha gods.
The Sudṛśa devas, Sudarśana devas, Sātata devas, Avṛha devas, Ekottaraśuddha devas, Ākāśānantyāyatana devas,
Vijñānānantyāyatana devas, Ākiṃcanyāyatana devas, and Naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatana devas all gathered together;
the bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, kumārakas, and kumārikās were beyond reckoning.
The calculations were also all brought together, and from the thousands of worlds throughout the ten directions, they all came and stood before the high seat.

At that time, the Bodhisattva Awakening Mind (Jueyi), seeing that the great assembly had all gathered, relied upon the power of his own merit, the power of his firm resolve, the power of dhāraṇī, the power of analytical eloquence, the power of fearlessness, and the majestic power of honoring the Buddha; he took up ten billion difficult questions before the Buddha amidst the assembly, and for each question, he produced and dispatched ten billion meanings to resolve them. Without changing the timing, without shifting from his seat, and without rising or moving his knees or feet, what he spoke flowed smoothly with meanings free of error; those who heard it were suddenly enlightened, as if seeing light in the darkness.

At that time, sixty thousand people in the assembly all resolved their minds upon the unsurpassed, true, and right path; eighty-four thousand bodhisattvas attained the patience regarding the non-arising of dharmas.
The Tathāgata Śāntamūrdhan then praised him, saying:
"Excellent, excellent!

At that moment, his voice resounded throughout the trichiliocosm; from the earth spirits below up to the assembly of the Śuddhāvāsa deities above, all heard the sound and together exclaimed in admiration:
"This Bodhisattva is now able to resolve ten billion difficult questions; he shall be named Zhijī (Accumulation of Wisdom).
Son of Good Family, it is for this reason that he is called Zhijī."
"If you wish to know who that Bodhisattva Awakening-Mind was at that time,
do not think it was anyone else. Why is this so?
"This is indeed the Bodhisattva Jñānākara.
Chapter Twenty-Seven: The Chapter on Praise from the *Mahākaruṇā-sūtra*. Then, the Bodhisattva Sarvaśūra came before the Buddha and addressed him, saying, "It is unprecedented! It is marvelous!"
World-Honored One!

Only the Buddhas, the Heroes of the World, are able to skillfully resolve this pure, supreme, and true path of enlightenment; they can eloquently expound its immeasurable words and phrases, enter its limitless meanings that are difficult to receive and uphold, and comprehend the profound and subtle twelvefold dependent origination. It is also extremely difficult for those who cannot apply themselves to diligent study to master it, and among those who practice the two paths, none are able to equal them.

These six sense-faculties are difficult to extinguish; because one sits bound by attachments, they cannot be liberated through expedient means. This is not something that can be attained by those of inferior capacity on the stages of the Śrāvakas or Pratyekabuddhas.

"This Bodhisattva practices the seal that encompasses all phenomena; when he surveys the dharma-realm, he does so with equanimity, just like space, free from the notion of agency and entirely without attachment."

Transcending all expectations and distinguishing the various conducts of sentient beings, they clearly understand the conditions of all retributions and further proclaim the Perfection of Wisdom; extensively cultivating skillful means, they uphold the state of tranquil stillness and attain supernormal powers.
Because their practice is equal, they enter the single gate of the Buddha without distinction or differentiation, not making it manifold.
Their equanimity is like space; it has no peer, and its equality is such that there is nothing with which it can be equalized.

All Buddhas are equal and free from duality; they practice the tranquility of cessation and eliminate all words and letters. They guide others toward the meaning so that it may be discerned and understood, yet while their resonance resounds, no [fixed] meaning can be grasped.

Having attained equal cultivation, they practice the service of the Triple Gem, expound the three gates of liberation, transcend the triple world, and clearly understand the three types of perfect penetration, giving rise to sovereign mastery.
By means of the concentration of meditative absorption, they are able to establish the Dharma of all Buddhas; harboring the Buddha-wisdom, they benefit all beings and are praised by all Buddhas.
“Yes, indeed, World-Honored One!

If sons or daughters of good family are able to have faith in these Buddhas of the past, future, and present, and in such analogies as these—the principles of the Way taught by them and their immeasurable wisdom—and if, through this faithful joy, they resolve to attain the unsurpassed, right, and true path and protect the True Dharma; and if, upon hearing the essentials of such sūtras as these, they uphold, recite, read, and fully explain them to others, thereby attaining boundless merit, then they shall be considered to have repaid the kindness of the Tathāgata with filial piety and gratitude.”
The Buddha said: "So it is, so it is,
son of good family!"
It is as you have said.

If a son of noble family or a daughter of noble family were to behold with their own eyes the lands manifested by the Buddhas of the ten directions and, filling them with the seven treasures, offer them as gifts to the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas; yet if there were another person who, holding this sūtra, diligently recites and reads it, fully expounds it, proclaims it to the assembly, zealously and energetically receives and masters this orthodox canon, and carries it forth in practice without violating or severing the teachings of the Triple Gem—the virtue of such a practitioner would surpass the former beyond measure.
At that time, after the World-Honored One had spoken this meaning, he uttered these verses:
"With my Buddha-eye, I behold all lands; The Tathāgatas therein are like heaps of purple gold."
If one makes offerings to the Tathāgata, the merit is still meager; yet if one hears this scripture, the merit is vast.
Those who are worthy vessels and are able to hear this sutra—profound, mysterious, and sublime, the foremost and most ultimate truth—[attain immeasurable benefit].
Having fully attained it, one immediately receives it; by upholding, reciting, and reading it, one calculates this merit and virtue as the most supreme and honored.
Most excellent is this: one dwells eternally in the Dharma and sustains life through the Dharma, not through clothing or food.
"Therefore, you should uphold and dwell securely in the Dharma; this is true filial piety, and it is how one repays the kindness of all Buddhas.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the assembly of all the bodhisattvas gathered there:
"Who among you is capable of receiving and protecting this unsurpassed, truly correct path of the Dharma of all the Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, of the past, future, and present?"

After my parinirvāṇa, during the age of the five turbidities when worldly customs are tumultuous and chaotic, you shall be able to transmit this sutra so that it may spread widely, ensuring that the True Dharma remains and endures for a long time.
At that moment, the assembly of sixty trillion nayutas of bodhisattvas simultaneously raised their voices and uttered this eulogy:
"O World-Honored One! We..."

Throughout countless billions of kalpas, across hundreds of thousands of nayutas, you have accumulated this unsurpassed, true, and correct teaching of the Way; in future ages, you shall widely proclaim it.
Furthermore, O Great Sage, please bestow your majestic grace and establish your divine virtue,
so that this sutra may be widely disseminated in the future final age;
and cause all classes of sentient beings to together receive and uphold its command, proclaiming it to the people.
"One who has planted the roots of virtue;
one who has already accumulated merit—such a person alone shall be able to hear it.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke this verse in praise:
“The Perfectly Awakened One’s words are sincere; abiding in the Dharma of ultimate truth, he establishes these sincere words and conforms to this sutra.
He dwells in inexhaustible compassion and resides in boundless loving-kindness.”
Manifesting compassion for sentient beings, he therefore established this sutra;
Accomplishing the chapter on merit and virtue, surpassing the ranks of all noble wisdoms,
and universally entering into all modes of conduct, he therefore established this sutra.
Having subdued all Māras, dissolved all heterodox teachings,
and destroyed all false views, this sutra was established;
the Four Kings, Śakra Devendra, and Brahmā King expound upon generosity.
Devas, nāgas, and gandharvas have established this sūtra;
earth spirits, celestial beings of the void, and all the various minor deities—
seeing what has been established by the name of the Buddha, they shall uphold this decree.
Cultivating the four Brahma-vihāras, adorned by the four truths themselves,
and protecting those within his domain, he has therefore established this sutra.
Though space is devoid of form and appearance, he causes that which is formless to possess form.
"What the Buddha has established, none can move or alter.
At that time, the Four Heavenly Kings, with one voice and in different mouths, praised the Buddha before him in verse:
"We shall follow this scripture, protected by the Buddha’s majestic power."
Their descendants and retinues shall likewise follow and attend them.
If there are those who uphold [this teaching] and apply themselves diligently to the Way and its teachings,
we shall serve them and provide protection on all four sides.
Then Śakra, Lord of the Devas, recited this verse before the Buddha:
"We shall repay the Buddha’s kindness And protect the Dharma of the Teacher;
This wondrous and sublime sutra— By practicing it, one attains Buddhahood."
"We shall serve as the Buddhas' filial heirs, protecting and upholding this sutra;
by nourishing and cherishing such a scripture, we shall thereby uphold the Dharma.
Then, the Brahmā Śikhin, before the Buddha, uttered these verses in praise:
Those who do not practice heedlessness shall transcend all vehicles;
they are all born from this sutra, which contains profound and peerless meaning.
One should renounce even the bliss of the Brahma heavens wherever this sutra resides.
"Therefore, you should go to listen and receive [the teaching], and you should also provide protection accordingly.
At that time, the Deva-king Tuṣita spoke these verses before the Buddha:
"He who is in his final birth for enlightenment descends from Tuṣita;
I shall then uphold these scriptures spoken by the Buddha.
World-Honored One!
I am capable of renouncing celestial bliss to dwell and travel throughout Jambudvīpa, so that I may hear and study this scripture.
Then the son of Māra, the Teacher, spoke these verses before the Buddha:
"Having brought an end to the karmic offenses of Māra, He shall no longer follow those who harm the Teaching;
Whoever upholds this sutra Shall understand its meaning and practice accordingly."
"I shall protect this scripture of the Tathāgata,
causing them to arouse diligence and enabling them all to attain it fully.
At that time, Māra Pāpīyas recited these verses before the World-Honored One:
"Among the classes of sentient beings, I shall no longer cause ruin or disorder.
Those who receive and uphold this [teaching] will gather and destroy the dust of manifold desires;
no māras shall find an opportunity against them."
"Those who preach this sutra are established by all Buddhas; I shall protect and sustain them.
Thereupon, the Devaputra Susīma, in the presence of the World-Honored One, uttered these verses in praise:
"The true path of all Buddhas is fully expounded in this sutra."
If there be those who uphold this sutra, they shall then serve all Buddhas.
I shall grasp this scripture and, for the sake of billions of devas, praise it, exhorting and assisting them to resolve upon the Way;
those who hear it shall then follow and practice it.
Thereupon, Maitreya Bodhisattva, before the World-Honored One, uttered these verses in praise:
"If one possesses resolve and the Way, Their compassion need not depend on others;
They protect all dharmas, And spontaneously give from their own will."
"I shall go to the Tuṣita Heaven, where the Buddha has established these true and semblance sūtras, and cause them to be widely disseminated.
Thereupon, the Elder Mahākāśyapa uttered this verse in the presence of the World-Honored One:
"We are of meager wisdom and little learning;
we shall rely upon the power of what the Śrāvakas have taught to uphold the Dharma of the World-Honored One.
If there be anyone who receives and upholds this, we shall go to attend and protect them."
"It is worthy of being proclaimed with eloquence; I praise it, saying, 'Excellent!
Then, in the presence of the World-Honored One, Śāriputra uttered this verse in praise:
"The Dharma is like empty space, as taught by the Protector of the World."
I shall nurture and sustain it, reverently honoring this sublime scripture.
In whatever region one upholds such a sutra as this,
dwelling in future ages, they shall protect and cherish all their kin.
Then the elder Mahāmaudgalyāyana, in the presence of the World-Honored One, uttered this verse in praise:
“The World-Honored One now dwells in the present, purifying all sentient beings;
by upholding this sutra, they examine its meaning and practice it with insight.”
Throughout hundreds of thousands of kalpas, he shall never return to the evil realms;
having already received the Buddha’s prophecy, he has become a prince of the Dharma.
Thereupon, the Venerable Ānanda, before the World-Honored One, uttered these verses in praise:
"Face to face before the Buddha, I have heard tens of thousands of sūtras;
yet from the very beginning, I have never before heard a sūtra such as this.
Having now encountered this scripture, I have personally received it through consultation with the Sage."
"You should cause it to be widely disseminated for those who seek the path of the Buddha.
At that time, the World-Honored One praised Śakra, Brahmā, the Four Heavenly Kings, and all the devaputras, bodhisattvas, and śrāvakas:
"Excellent, excellent!"
Virtuous and upright sirs!
You are indeed able to protect the true Dharma and likewise proclaim the lion’s roar.
Now I earnestly entrust and commit this to you, O virtuous ones.

If there are those among the multitude whose minds are set upon the Mahāyāna but who have not yet attained the patience of the Dharma (*dharmakṣānti*), should they encounter such established scriptures and receive them, recite, or read them, they will always be face-to-face with the Tathāgata; in this way, before long they shall receive their prediction and achieve the unsurpassed, right, and true path.
If those who study as Śrāvakas receive this sūtra from the Buddha, they shall be numbered among the first assembly of the Maitreya Tathāgata, the True One.
If those of the Pratyekabuddha vehicle maintain, recite, or read these scriptures, then even after my parinirvāṇa, though they hear nothing further, they shall achieve the path of a Pratyekabuddha.

When the Buddha had spoken these meanings from the *Sūtra of the Questions of the Bodhisattva Sarvashura*, countless people all resolved their minds upon the unsurpassed, right, and true path; incalculable multitudes of bodhisattvas established themselves on the stage of non-retrogression; and an inexpressible number of bodhisattvas attained the patience regarding the non-arising of all phenomena (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*).
Infinite worlds shook in six ways, a great radiance pervaded the ten directions, and the heavens rained down various flowers.

The bodhisattvas who had gathered from the ten directions offered worship to the Buddha, reverently honoring the True Dharma and adorning the high seats with all manner of jewels. They manifested precious flowers and, raising their voices in unison, proclaimed his merits:

"We have attained excellent benefit and boundless joy; having personally approached and arrived here, we have heard this sūtra that resolves doubts. We pray that the World-Honored One Śākyamuni may prolong his life and remain long in the world, so that this sūtra may forever circulate universally throughout Jambudvīpa."

Those bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, kumārakas, and kumārikās who receive and uphold such sūtras as these shall likewise be granted protection; they shall also be endowed with long life, and by constantly bestowing great benefit upon sentient beings, all shall attain liberation through these conditions.
Chapter 28: Entrustment. In the *Mahākaruṇā-sūtra*, Chapter Twenty-Eight, "Entrustment," the Bodhisattva Sarvashūra then addressed the Buddha, saying:
"It is truly unprecedented."

The World-Honored One has skillfully analyzed and expounded the meaning of this sutra; what he has proclaimed is subtle and its phrasing is brilliant. It is that which the foremost of Bodhisattvas should practice: subduing all Māras and heterodox teachers, employing expedient means to guide and direct various scriptures according to the times, thereby delighting the hearts of sentient beings, giving rise to the practices of all vehicles, fully entering the boundless merits of the Tathāgata, personally fulfilling all vows, and manifesting the Great Way.
"What is the name of this sutra,
and how should it be practiced?
The Buddha told the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra:

“This sutra is titled ‘The Great Compassion of the Tathāgata’; you should uphold it as the teaching proclaimed by the Buddha. Having heard the Tathāgata’s excellent predictions, which have never been false, you should uphold them.”

When the Buddha had spoken thus, the Bodhisattva Sarvaśūra, the bodhisattvas gathered from the worlds of the ten directions, the great disciples, Śakra, Brahmā, and the Four Heavenly Kings, as well as devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, male novices, and female novices—the entire assembly of devas and humans—heard what the Buddha had said and were all filled with joy.
The Scripture of Great Compassion, Scroll Eight.
